criteria.ambient_scope: Dispatch installs a per-request scope holding the shared budget, an abort signal, and an escalation collector; every SQL and fetch adapter consults that scope without new call arguments, so a disconnect or shutdown expires each in-flight operation individually with its own unknown-write outcome plus escalation record, while an explicit caller bound still takes the minimum with the remaining budget.
criteria.outer_race: Dispatch only races the entire handler against the request budget; when the budget wins it sends one bounded response and files a single request-level escalation while the handler keeps draining silently, so inner operations settle without ever producing their own unknown-write outcome or escalation record.

propagation.instructions: Which propagation shape should carry disconnect and shutdown expiry from dispatch into running operations?

criteria.new_failure: Introduce a fresh catalogue failure such as sql::operation_unknown and append it to the emits union of every budgeted SQL call, making boundary expiry explicit in the checked error union at the cost of catalogue regeneration, checker and emitter updates, and migration of existing examples by other lanes.
criteria.reuse_query_failed: Report SQL boundary expiry through the already emitted sql::query_failed failure with a documented code string (the operation field names the call, code carries budget); no catalogue, checker, or emitter edit is needed, Can handlers match on the code, and the adapter lowers the shared unknown-write marker into this domain value.

sql_failure.instructions: Which failure shape should a SQL operation return when the visible boundary gives up at its bound while the native query stays owned?

criteria.status_400: Answer a bound-expired ingress body read with the same fixed 400 already used for body read errors, leaving the rejected-status union untouched and treating stalls exactly like corrupt bodies.
criteria.status_408: Answer a bound-expired ingress body read with a fixed 408 Request Timeout, extending the rejected-status union with 408 while read errors keep returning 400 and over-limit bodies keep returning 413.

stall_status.instructions: Which status should bounded ingress return when the body read outlasts its stall bound?

state: Can is a server language whose generated TypeScript adapters run on Bun 1.4.2 and call native operations directly. Measured probes fix the design space: Bun.SQL Query.cancel flips a client flag only on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite while every backend runs to completion, and cancelling before execution never settles, so SQL takes the cancel-absent branch where the visible boundary returns at the operation bound, the native query stays owned until settlement, and the outcome is honestly unknown with supervisor escalation. Bun.serve Request.signal aborts promptly on peer disconnect but stops nothing by itself, so it is observation only. The finished E01 layer provides one shared request budget per request with effective deadline min(own bound, remaining budget), a frozen unknown-write marker of commit unknown plus owned plus supervisor escalation shared across SQL, fetch, actions, S3, and workers, drain-by-default closing, and leases that no timer revokes. Interface rules require finite explicit emits unions, one unknown-write vocabulary, and no caller operand without a verified native meaning; checker and emitter edits belong to other lanes while this task owns runtime code, tests, and catalogue merges for its own sections. Already emitted failures include sql::query_failed with operation and code strings, sql::commit_unknown with a transaction id on the transaction path, http::timeout with timeout_ms, and http::transport_failed with a phase string. Server ingress currently drains request bodies without any bound, mapping read errors to fixed 400 and oversize bodies to fixed 413; there are zero external users and no compatibility obligation.
